warmup.description: Activate shoulders, upper back, and core while gradually increasing pressing and pulling readiness.
movements: Dead hang or assisted hang x 20-30s

main_exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a weight that feels like an 8/10 effort, leaving 1-2 reps in reserve
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep shoulder blades pinned and lower the bar with control to mid-chest

main_exercises.name: Pull-Ups (assisted or weighted)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose assistance or load so the last 2 reps are challenging but controlled
main_exercises.form_cue: Lead with your chest and avoid swinging your legs

main_exercises.name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate-heavy load at 7-8/10 effort, maintain strict form throughout
main_exercises.form_cue: Brace core and press straight overhead without arching your lower back

main_exercises.name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use a weight that challenges your upper back without compromising posture
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep a flat back and pull the bar toward your lower ribs

main_exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Chest Press
main_exercises.load_guidance: Select a weight you could perform 12 reps with, stopping at 8-10
main_exercises.form_cue: Control the descent and avoid locking out aggressively at the top

main_exercises.name: Superset: Dumbbell Bicep Curl + Tricep Dips
main_exercises.load_guidance: Use moderate weight for curls and bodyweight or assisted dips at steady effort
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep elbows stable during curls and shoulders down during dips

cooldown.description: Release tension in the upper body and restore shoulder mobility.
movements: Chest stretch against wall x 30s each side
Child’s pose with arms extended x 45s
Cross-body shoulder stretch x 30s each side

phase_notes.menstrual: You may want to reduce load slightly on compound lifts like bench press and overhead press while keeping movement quality high. Focus on controlled reps and longer rest if energy is lower.
phase_notes.follicular: This is a great phase to push intensity in lifts like bench press and pull-ups—aim to progressively increase load or reps. You’ll likely feel more explosive and capable of handling volume.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Take advantage of peak strength and coordination by pushing your heaviest sets here, especially on compound lifts. Just be mindful of joint stability and maintain strict form.
phase_notes.early_luteal: You can still train hard here, but prioritize consistency over max effort—keep loads challenging but avoid grinding reps. This is a good time to reinforce solid technique under fatigue.
phase_notes.late_luteal: This high-intensity session may feel more taxing—consider reducing volume (fewer sets) or slightly lowering load while maintaining structure. Focus on moving well rather than pushing limits.
